scope: Source-verified pediatric antibiotic regimens by syndrome
rule: This registry is syndrome-specific. It is not a universal antibiotic table. Selection still requires diagnosis, age, allergy, renal function, culture history and resistance context.

entries.syndrome: suspected community-acquired sepsis, age >=28 days and <16 years
entries.source: NICE NG254, updated 2025: 80 mg/kg once daily, max 4 g, excluding newborns under 28 days

entries.syndrome: community-acquired sepsis in newborn under 28 days, only if >40 weeks corrected gestational age and not receiving IV calcium
community-acquired sepsis in newborn under 28 days when ceftriaxone criteria not met

entries.source: NICE NG111: age 3 months to 11 years up to 50 kg, 50-80 mg/kg once daily, max 4 g/day

entries.syndrome: acute pyelonephritis, age >=3 months; use when indicated by susceptibility/combination guidance
entries.source: NICE NG111: 30 mg/kg three times daily, max 1.2 g per dose

entries.syndrome: acute pyelonephritis, age >=3 months, IV option
entries.frequency: initial dose once daily; subsequent doses by serum concentration and renal function

entries.syndrome: acute pyelonephritis, age >=3 months, IV option
entries.frequency: initial dose once daily; subsequent doses by serum concentration and renal function

entries.syndrome: lower UTI, age 3 months to 11 years, low resistance risk
lower UTI, age 3 months to 11 years, eGFR >=45 mL/min
cellulitis/erysipelas, penicillin allergy or flucloxacillin unsuitable, age 1 month to 11 years
entries.source: NICE NG141; weight-based dose is explicit for children under 8 kg and IV for 1 month-11 years; oral older-child bands remain age/weight-band based

entries.syndrome: suspected bacterial meningitis, age beyond neonatal pathway
entries.frequency: start within 1 h of hospital arrival
entries.source: NICE NG240 2024: ceftriaxone first choice; use highest BNFC dose. Exact pediatric dose is intentionally not duplicated here because NG240 delegates it to BNFC.
